title: endsWith
summary: Test whether text inputs end with patterns in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Runs on the host. Numeric resident subject or pattern values are not text and reject before provider access; a resident IgnoreCase control is a compatibility-gated RunMat extension.

description: `endsWith(str, pattern)` returns one logical result for each element of `str`. When `pattern` has multiple elements, each element is an alternative and a subject matches if any pattern is a suffix.
behaviors: Accepts text inputs as string scalars/arrays, character vectors/arrays, or cell arrays of character vectors.
Accepts patterns in the same formats. Multiple patterns form an alternatives set rather than an element-wise array paired with `str`.
Missing string scalars (`<missing>`) never match any pattern.
Empty patterns (`""` or `''`) always match non-missing text elements.
Patterns that are `<missing>` never match and therefore return `false`.
Character arrays treat each row as an independent element; zero-row character arrays yield empty outputs.

MATLAB-compatible mode accepts the documented `'IgnoreCase', logical` name-value form. RunMat mode additionally supports a positional flag and numeric or textual predicate values behind explicit extension gates.
Returns a logical scalar for a scalar subject and otherwise returns a logical array with the shape of `str`.

examples.description: Check if a filename ends with an extension
Apply a scalar suffix to every element of a string array
Test every subject against a set of suffixes
Test suffixes for a cell array of character vectors
Handle empty patterns and missing values

faqs.question: What types can I pass to `endsWith`?
faqs.answer: Use string arrays, character vectors, or cell arrays of character vectors for both arguments. Every pattern is tested as an alternative against each subject element.

faqs.question: How do I ignore letter case?
faqs.answer: MATLAB-compatible mode uses `'IgnoreCase', true` or false. RunMat mode additionally accepts textual values such as `'on'` and a positional flag behind explicit extension gates. The option name is case-insensitive.

faqs.question: What happens with empty patterns?
faqs.answer: Empty patterns (`""` or `''`) always match non-missing text elements. When the text element is missing (`<missing>`), the result is `false`.

faqs.question: Can I provide multiple suffixes at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Provide `pattern` as a string array, character vector, cell array of character vectors, or supported pattern object. A subject returns true when any supplied pattern is a suffix.

faqs.question: How are missing strings treated?
faqs.answer: Missing string scalars (displayed as `<missing>`) never match any pattern and produce `false` in the result. Use `ismissing` if you need to handle missing values separately.

faqs.question: Does `endsWith` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. Text values are host-resident. Numeric resident subject and pattern values reject before provider access. RunMat mode can gather an explicitly compatibility-gated resident IgnoreCase control.

faqs.question: Does `endsWith` preserve the input shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. The output has the shape of `str`; pattern-array shape does not change it. A scalar subject produces a logical scalar.

gpu_residency: `endsWith` executes on host text. Numeric resident subject or pattern values reject before provider access. A resident scalar IgnoreCase control is available only in RunMat mode and is gathered after its extension gate succeeds.
gpu_behavior: `endsWith` performs host-side suffix comparison. It has no numeric GPU data path or fusion hook; only a compatibility-gated resident scalar control can cross the provider boundary.
